comment: Authored PROVIDER responses for the mutation-overlap case. Tool-plan requests decline; edit-plan requests are keyed by the turn token embedded in each ask. Find-strings extracted VERBATIM from the frozen canvas's audit-first resolved revision. TOOL SCOPING (2026-09-28, F03): every entry now declares the tool it answers, so the shim selects by EXACT advertised tool name before falling back to a prompt substring. Measured: with substring-only selection, 12 of 16 CanvasEditPlan calls were served a ToolPlan decline because the two CanvasEditPlan entries carried no 'match' key at all and a catch-all substring ('Validation Error found') was consuming the edit-planner requests. The CanvasEditPlan entries therefore were never reachable. Tool scoping is harness selection only: it is not per-prompt routing and it does not change production dispatch. TOOL+DISCRIMINATOR SELECTION (2026-09-28, F03): each plan answers CanvasEditPlan, so a bare tool key left only the last one reachable and every edit-planner request was served the OVLAP-B plan, whose `find` text is absent from the canvas. Both plans now carry the request ref present in their own prompt and are keyed (tool, match); the shim prefers that pair over a bare tool hit. Still harness selection only -- not per-prompt routing, and no production dispatch change. F05: the negative control needs an actual execution FAILURE, not merely a missing target -- a missing target still gets satisfied by the tool fallback path. F12 (2026-09-29): the six read workflows include two plain-language turns that are not workbook reads. Without a scripted answer the shim returned 502 'no scripted response matched this request', which the case then had to distinguish from a product failure.

The row-group note in the canvas now carries the OVLAP-B marker.

responses.comment: F05 controlled EXECUTION FAILURE. wants_edit=True with zero ops is a plan-contract violation: the editor must refuse it, commit nothing, and let the background leg record an honest failure. Chosen because the ovlapref-b plan is NOT a negative control -- its `find` text is absent, but the marker was still added through the tool fallback path with the rest of the body intact, so it applied instead of failing.

responses.match: what is a price list used for
responses.response: A price list is a document that sets out the prices a seller charges for products or services, usually by part, model or tier.
Here is the same information in a plainer layout: one item per line, each with its part number, description and list price, and no repeating table headers.
